output.normalized_title: analytics-pipeline: S3 multipart upload rejected with QuotaExceeded (analytics-pipeline)
symptoms: S3 multipart upload rejected with QuotaExceeded

output.classification_reasoning: The failure is triggered by an S3 multipart upload being rejected with a QuotaExceeded error, which directly indicates that the storage quota for the analytics-pipeline's S3 bucket has been exhausted. This is a storage capacity issue rather than a network, application, authentication, or database problem. The incident impacted 150 users and lasted 14 minutes, suggesting that the quota breach was detected quickly but required investigation and remediation (e.g., increasing the quota or cleaning up space). The need to coordinate between the analytics pipeline, S3 bucket policies, and possibly downstream data consumers adds moderate operational effort, placing the incident in the 'Moderate' complexity tier.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
output.security_notes: Verify write freeze before node reboot. Promote read-replica prior to primary teardown.

recurring_patterns.symptom_pattern: analytics-pipeline: S3 multipart upload rejected with QuotaExceeded

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: Historical correlation indicates recurring pattern in analytics-pipeline.

output.justification: The incident impacts 150 users, exceeding the >=100 user threshold defined for a moderate disruption. The outage duration is 14 minutes, which falls within the acceptable window for Tier-3 services before escalation to higher severity. The diagnostic stage is "Root Cause Confirmed" with a high confidence score (0.95), and the issue aligns with a known recurring storage exhaustion pattern. According to corporate SLA policies, these conditions map directly to SEV-3.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Access and Kubernetes Context
remediation_steps.description: Ensure the operator has the required ProdOperations role and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster in us-east-1.
verification: Current context string contains 'prod-us-east-1'
AWS caller identity ARN matches the ProdOperations role

remediation_steps.title: Assess Storage Utilization and Identify Exhaustion Sources
remediation_steps.description: Query S3 bucket metrics and pod volume usage to confirm the storage exhaustion root cause and locate the offending prefixes.
commands: aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/S3 --metric-name BucketSizeBytes --dimensions Name=BucketName,Value=analytics-pipeline-data --statistics Average --period 300 --start-time $(date -u -d '-1h' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
kubectl exec -n analytics $(kubectl get pod -l app=analytics-pipeline -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- df -h
verification: S3 bucket size reported > 90% of allocated quota
Pod volume usage > 85% of PVC capacity
List of large objects returned for further cleanup

remediation_steps.title: Enforce Write Freeze on Analytics Pipeline
remediation_steps.description: Temporarily block new write operations to prevent further storage consumption while remediation proceeds.
verification: ConfigMap key WRITE_FREEZE is set to "true"
All analytics-pipeline pods report annotation write-freeze=enabled

remediation_steps.title: Promote Read‑Replica to Primary for the Backend Store
remediation_steps.description: Promote the standby replica (RDS or DynamoDB) to become the writable primary before any primary node is taken down.
verification: RDS instance status changes to 'available' and role = primary
DynamoDB table shows StreamEnabled=true

remediation_steps.title: Perform Controlled Node Reboot
remediation_steps.description: Cordon and drain the affected worker node, then issue a reboot via AWS SSM. This clears any lingering filesystem locks after the write freeze.
commands: aws ssm send-command --instance-ids $(aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=private-dns-name,Values=<node-name> --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].InstanceId' --output text) --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --parameters commands='sudo reboot'
verification: Node shows NotReady status during drain
Node returns to Ready status after reboot
No pods remain in CrashLoopBackOff on the node

remediation_steps.title: Remove Write Freeze and Validate Service Health
remediation_steps.description: Re‑enable writes, restart the deployment, and run health checks to confirm normal operation.
commands: kubectl logs -l app=analytics-pipeline --since=5m | grep ERR_STORAGE_EXHAUSTION_333 || echo 'No storage errors'
verification: ConfigMap WRITE_FREEZE is "false"
All pods report READY=1/1 and Running
Health endpoint returns HTTP 200 with body 'OK'
Log grep returns no storage exhaustion errors

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert any promotion, restore original write‑freeze state, and roll back the deployment to the pre‑remediation image tag. Verify storage metrics return to baseline before declaring rollback complete.

steps.description: Undo deployment image to previous tag
verification: Deployment revision rolls back to previous version
Pods start with the prior container image

steps.description: Demote promoted replica and re‑activate original primary
verification: Original primary reports status 'available' and role = primary
Promoted replica reverts to read‑only mode

steps.description: Remove write freeze (if still set) and ensure writes are enabled
verification: ConfigMap WRITE_FREEZE key equals "false"

commands: aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/S3 --metric-name BucketSizeBytes --dimensions Name=BucketName,Value=analytics-pipeline-data --statistics Average --period 300 --start-time $(date -u -d '-30m' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
verification: Bucket size < 80% of quota for two consecutive checks

prerequisite_checks: Operator credentials verified for ProdOperations role
Write‑freeze policy documented and approved by change management
Rollback procedures reviewed and stored in the runbook repository
